title: Egypt Mourns Flynas Attendant Azza Ramzy as Funeral Is Held in Beheira
excerpt: The 28-year-old's body arrived in Alexandria late on Monday after she died of injuries sustained in the October 10 attack on Riyadh's airport, which killed people from at least eight countries.
body:
• Mourners in Egypt's Beheira governorate have bid farewell to Azza Ramzy Mohamed Hassan, a 28-year-old Egyptian flight attendant with Saudi airline flynas who died of injuries sustained in the October 10 attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.
  • Her body arrived at Alexandria International Airport late on Monday and was taken to al-Atf, in the Mahmoudiya district of Beheira, for the funeral procession, according to Egyptian reporting.
  • Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said the October 10 attack killed 12 people and injured 309; the toll later rose to 13 when an Indian national died of his injuries.
  • Egypt condemned the attack, said five other Egyptians were injured, and directed its embassy and consulate in Riyadh to repatriate her body and support the injured.

Mourners in Beheira, Egypt, have bid farewell to Azza Ramzy Mohamed Hassan, a 28-year-old flight attendant killed in the Houthi attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, according to Al Jazeera. Hassan worked for the Saudi airline flynas and was on duty in the terminal when the airport was struck on Saturday, October 10. She died of her injuries.

Her body comes home

Egyptian reporting carried by Al-Masry Al-Youm said her body arrived at Alexandria International Airport at about 11:30 p.m. on Monday aboard a flynas aircraft from al-Qassim, in Saudi Arabia. Civil Aviation Minister Sameh al-Hefny oversaw the arrival, her family was present to receive the remains, and the family then took the body to the al-Atf area of Mahmoudiya, in Beheira, for the funeral procession.

Hassan was a native of Atf village in the Mahmoudiya district, according to the same reporting. Beheira Governor Jacqueline Azer offered condolences to her family, relatives and the community of al-Atf, and neighbours had gathered outside the family home on Sunday and Monday to offer condolences. Flynas published a formal obituary confirming her death and paid tribute to her dedication and to the reputation she left among colleagues, according to reporting on the airline's statement.

Egypt's response

Egypt's foreign ministry condemned the attack on Sunday, identified Hassan by name, and said five other Egyptian nationals were injured. According to Daily News Egypt, Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty, acting on instructions from President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi, directed the Egyptian embassy and consulate in Riyadh to contact her family and expedite the repatriation of her body. The ministry also said Egypt's ambassador and consul visited the five injured Egyptians in hospital and were coordinating with Saudi authorities on their care.

A multinational toll

Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said the October 10 attack killed 12 people and injured 309. The dead included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, and one national each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. The Associated Press reported that the toll rose to 13 after India's embassy in Saudi Arabia said an Indian national died on Sunday of injuries sustained in Saturday's attack. The airport was struck again on Sunday, and the terminal has remained closed, disrupting flights across the region, including services by Indian carriers.

The victims reflect the multinational workforce and travelling public that pass through Riyadh's airport every day: airline crew, migrant workers and passengers from across South Asia, the Middle East and beyond. Hassan's funeral in Beheira follows a similar moment of grief for an Indian family — the family of a Hyderabad man killed in the same attack decided to hold his funeral in Saudi Arabia, as The Videshi reported earlier this week. One Indian national died and three others were treated in intensive care after the attack, in a case The Videshi covered here.

What's next

The Houthis claimed responsibility for the attacks on the airport, and the Saudi-led coalition blamed the group for the strike. The airport closure has been extended as Saudi Arabia tracks further drone and missile threats, and Indian airlines have cancelled Saudi flights through October 17, as The Videshi reported here. For Hassan's family in Mahmoudiya, the wider confrontation has already produced its final outcome: a daughter flown home at night, and a funeral in the village she came from.
